summary: ראש is the head: the head of a body, then whatever is at the top or the front of anything, the top of a mountain or a tower, the chief over a people or a house, the start of a month or a watch, the sum of a count, and the choicest of a kind. רִאשׁוֹן is what comes first in order or time, “the first month” of the feasts (Lev 23:5) or the former days, and Yahweh calls himself רִאשׁוֹן and אַחֲרוֹן, the first and the last (Isa 44:6). רֵאשִׁית is the beginning (Gen 1:1) and the first part of a thing, above all the first of the harvest brought to Yahweh, the sheaf of Lev 23:10. The New Testament calls Christ the head of the corner, the head of his body, and the firstfruits of those who sleep, and the Peshitta writes these with the same root, רִישָׁא and רִשִׁיתָא. Arabic raʾs, Ugaritic riš, Akkadian rēšu, Phoenician rʾš and Ge'ez rəʾs all mean “head”.

doctrine.statement: Israel brought the first (רֵאשִׁית) of the harvest to Yahweh before any of it was eaten: the sheaf of Lev 23:10–14, the first of the dough, of the grain, oil and fleece (Num 15:20–21; Deu 18:4; Deu 26:2, 10). What was first was holy to Yahweh, and Israel itself was “holiness to Yahweh, the first of his harvest” (Jer 2:3). Paul writes that Christ has been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who sleep, and that each will be raised in order, Christ the firstfruits, then those who are Christ's at his coming (1Co 15:20–23). The Peshitta's word there is רִשִׁיתָא, the Hebrew רֵאשִׁית in Syriac, and in Paul's defence before Agrippa it says the Messiah would suffer and be the רִשִׁיתָא of the resurrection from the dead (Act 26:23). So the first of the harvest is a pledge of the rest: “if the firstfruit is holy, so is the lump” (Rom 11:16, from Num 15:20–21). Those who believe are also called firstfruits: begotten by the word of truth to be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures (Jas 1:18), redeemed from among men as firstfruits to God and to the Lamb (Rev 14:4), having the firstfruits of the Spirit while they wait for the redemption of the body (Rom 8:23). (The waving of the sheaf and its day are under the omer entry; the בִּכּוּרִים under the bakar entry.)

“The stone the builders rejected has become the head (רֹאשׁ) of the corner; this is from Yahweh” (Psa 118:22–23). Jesus quoted it of himself to the chief priests and elders (Mat 21:42), and Peter told the rulers that Jesus, whom they crucified and God raised, is that stone, rejected by them as builders, which has become the head of the corner (Act 4:10–11; 1Pe 2:7). Paul says God raised Christ from the dead, seated him at his right hand, put all things under his feet, and gave him to be head over all things to the assembly, which is his body (Eph 1:20–23); believers are to grow up in all things into him who is the head (Eph 4:15). He is the head of the body, the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, so that in all things he might be first (Col 1:18): in the Peshitta “head” and “beginning” there are both רִישָׁא. The order of headship goes up to God: the head of every man is Christ, and the head of Christ is God (1Co 11:3). The rejected one was made head by Yahweh, after his death and by his resurrection.

Yahweh says, “I am first (רִאשׁוֹן) and I am last, and besides me there is no god” (Isa 44:6; Isa 41:4; Isa 48:12): he was before all things and will remain after them, and his purpose runs from beginning to end (Isa 46:10). In the revelation God gave to Jesus (Rev 1:1), the risen Jesus says, “I am the first and the last, and the living one; I was dead, and behold, I am alive for ever” (Rev 1:17–18; Rev 2:8; Rev 22:13). The words Yahweh used of himself are spoken by the one he raised from death.

“The fear of Yahweh is the beginning (רֵאשִׁית) of knowledge; fools despise wisdom and instruction” (Pro 1:7), and “the beginning of wisdom is the fear of Yahweh; a good understanding have all who do them” (Psa 111:10). Knowing anything rightly starts with standing in awe of Yahweh; it is the first part, as the first of the harvest is, and the rest follows from it.

note: Left out: the gentilic/proper name רֹאשׁ (t.ad.al, Rosh of Ezk 38:2–3, 39:1, whose 608 tokens BDB lists identically with t.ad.aa) and רֹאשׁ the son of Benjamin (t.ad.ak, Gen 46:21; that key also holds Lam 3:19 by spelling, which belongs to the venom word). Keys with no tokens (m.di.aj, t.ab.at, t.ad.af, t.bq.ad, t.cp.ad, t.er.ac) are cross-references to the words above and are not listed. Counts: t.ad.aj (venom) is counted by spelling and its 190 'uses' are almost all 'head'; the real venom tokens are the c. 12 verses cited. xt.aa.ac (Aramaic רֵאשׁ) also takes Pro 30:8 רֵאשׁ by spelling, which is 'poverty' (root רוש), not this word. The venom word: no cognate sharing the meaning was found; Wiktionary's 'hemlock' is modern usage. Whether it is the same word as 'head' (a plant named for its head?) is unproven; it stays under this spelling with the link marked unclear. Peshitta: SEDRA root ריש lexemes 3017 רישא (181 tokens), 3019 רישיתא (28), 3018 רישיא (4), 3541 רישנא (4), 3020 רישנותא (1, Jud 1:6, not entered). Syriac lemma pointing follows the SEDRA vocalisation as transliterated in bible.db; Payne Smith not consulted. Ugaritic riš page verified on the scan (Segert p. 200); Krahmalkov pp. 436 and 438 verified on the PDF; Dillmann col. 294 verified on the archive.org page image n170. Not entered, leads only: Sabaic rʾs¹ (Wiktionary; check Biella/SabaWeb); Akkadian ša rēši 'eunuch, courtier' behind סָרִיס (separate root entry, a loan). Open: (1) the omer entry's doctrine 'the-first-sheaf' already sets out Lev 23:10–16 with 1Co 15:20–23; this entry's 'christ-the-firstfruits' was written on the word רֵאשִׁית/רִשִׁיתָא to avoid repeating the day question — reviewer may prefer to merge or trim one. (2) Gen 1:1 בְּרֵאשִׁית and the Peshitta's בְּרִשִׁית in Jhn 1:1 are recorded as a fact on the Syriac word, not as doctrine; whether a doctrine on 'in the beginning' (with Pro 8:22, Col 1:18, Rev 3:14) belongs here is left for review. (3) Zec 4:7 הָאֶבֶן הָרֹאשָׁה and Psa 118:22 are both a 'head' stone; scripture does not link them, so no doctrine was drawn.
